question: What do we know about the generational wealth transfer, and how are these five preparing for it?

claims.text: Size and timing - Cerulli (research published 2025-10-29): Cerulli projects households will transfer $123.7 trillion to heirs ($105 trillion) and charities ($18 trillion) between now and 2048. It says wealth is now more likely to be held by older households.

Gen X, millennials and women - Cerulli (published 2025-10-29): Generation Xers are expected to inherit $39 trillion and Millennials $46 trillion. Women in the Baby Boomer and older generations are expected to receive $40 trillion in 'horizontal' transfers as they outlive their husbands. Women in younger generations are expected to receive $47 trillion of the wealth transferred intergenerationally.

Nature of the transfer - Cerulli (published 2025-10-29): Cerulli says most of the wealth owned by older generations will eventually be donated or passed to Gen X or Millennial heirs, an estimated total of $85 trillion. Its 2024 Private Wealth Management Executive Survey lists the top factors preventing HNW wealth transfer planning. Two are 'not comfortable sharing financial information with their children' (64%) and 'fear that children are not prepared to inherit wealth' (64%). Two more are 'inexperience with multi-generational wealth strategies' (56%) and 'clients are unwilling to give up control to the next generation' (44%).

Global view - UBS report (published 2026-04-22): UBS estimates USD 83 trillion in private wealth will change hands globally over the next two to three decades (foreword) and about two decades (introduction). It describes the transfer as a journey that unfolds over time, not a single event. This is a global estimate, a different scope from Cerulli's household figures.

Preparation - Schwab (2025 calls): On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), management said 33% of new-to-firm retail households were under 30 and more than 50% under 40. It said higher-net-worth clients are 70% of retail assets. On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), management said it was enhancing tax, trust and estate capabilities, including plans to offer wealth.com's estate planning tools to retail clients. On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), the CEO said client assets are more concentrated among older generations today, while the average age of clients continues to get younger.

Preparation - Schwab (3Q26 call, October 2026): The CEO said approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials. He said roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high-net-worth and high-net-worth households, and that Schwab is 'well positioned to continue serving future generations when that wealth is passed on.' He said its 'retention rate around wealth transfers is extremely high.' The 3Q26 deck shows ~70% of NTF retail households as Gen Z and Millennials, 80% of retail assets held by U/HNW households, and ~75% of assets retained in a wealth transfer event.

Preparation - Raymond James (2025 calls): The CEO said (2Q25 call, July 2025) about 370 advisors had completed or were enrolled in its Private Wealth Advisor Program. He said the firm focuses on education, training, accreditation and capabilities so advisors can meet the needs of their most sophisticated clients. On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), he said the private wealth advisor program and expanded alternative investments platform support advisors who focus on high-net-worth clients. Neither statement mentions the wealth transfer.
Preparation - Raymond James (investor day deck, published 2025-06-05): The recruiting section lists a 'Next gen advisor strategy' (a slide heading only, no detail).

Preparation - Raymond James (trade press, published 2026-09-29; indicative, not authoritative): A trade-press article says the firm's high-net-worth effort includes estate and charitable planning, lending, risk management and 'intergenerational wealth strategies.' It says nearly 450 advisors had earned the Raymond James Private Wealth Advisor designation as of September 2026, according to Raymond James. The designation was launched in September 2022 and covers households generally with at least $5 million in investable assets.

Preparation - Edward Jones (2Q25 10-Q, August 2025): The Partnership said net new assets decreased 10% versus 2Q24. It attributed the downward trend to higher outflows, citing factors including 'an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm.' The 6-month 10-Q adds that the net new asset decrease was attributable to existing clients.

Preparation - Edward Jones (3Q25 10-Q, November 2025): Net new assets decreased 4% in the first nine months of 2025. The firm said the outflows continue 'an increasing downward trend influenced by several factors, including an aging client base, generational wealth transfers outside the firm,' and others.

Preparation - Edward Jones (2025 10-K, March 2026): The firm names 'competition for clients and personnel in light of the evolving financial services industry and generational wealth transfer, changing client demographics, preferences and values' as a strategic risk. It says it addresses these risks through initiatives and continuing investment to attract and retain qualified talent, with a competitive compensation program for financial advisors.

Preparation - Edward Jones (2025 10-K, March 2026): The firm lists initiatives targeting new clients: High Net Worth, Workplace, and 'a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.' It also lists Financial Planning Services. It cautions that success depends on broad adoption by financial advisors, CSTPs and home office associates, and that it cannot reliably predict the timing or outcome.

adjacent.text: Merrill's recruiting page (content as of 2026-11-03) cites the 2025 Forbes 'Top Next-Gen Wealth Advisors Best-in-State' list. The list considered advisors born in 1986 or later with at least 4 years as an advisor. Bank of America's GWIM release (2026-07-14) reports 24 Merrill advisors on Financial Planning's 2026 Top 40 Brokers Under 40.
adjacent.differs_because: These are advisor recognitions for next-generation advisors, not client-side heir or wealth-transfer programs, and the release covers GWIM (Merrill plus the Private Bank).

adjacent.text: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), BofA's CFO said GWIM continued to add advisors through an extensive training program and experienced hiring, and about one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.
adjacent.differs_because: This is GWIM (Merrill plus the Private Bank) advisor-pipeline evidence, not a stated wealth-transfer or heir program.

adjacent.text: On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), Morgan Stanley's CEO said the firm retains 99% of its clients. He said 60% of advisor-led assets are with clients of 20-year average duration, 30% with clients of under 10 years, and 10% with clients of under two years.
adjacent.differs_because: These are general client-retention and tenure figures, not retention of heirs or assets in a wealth transfer.

adjacent.text: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Morgan Stanley's CFO described greater retention of vested Workplace assets and channel migration toward advice. She said this contributed to over $1 trillion of total assets in the adviser-led strategy.
adjacent.differs_because: This describes the Workplace-to-advice funnel, not generational wealth transfer or heirs.

adjacent.text: A trade-press article (2026-10-28) reports Schwab announced its advisor center would offer Wealth.com's Ester, an AI-powered tax and estate planning tool. It says the tool helps advisors with tax and estate conversations, including creating a visual mapping of beneficiaries. A limited version is free until February 2027, then fee-based. Schwab is a minority investor in Wealth.com.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative, and it describes a tool for independent advisors on Schwab's advisor center, not an explicit heir-retention program.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - preparation for the generational wealth transfer: not found in the evidence provided. No Morgan Stanley passage names the wealth transfer, heirs or next-gen client programs.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management investor materials, 10-K Item 1 and earnings call Q&A on next-generation/heir retention

gaps.what: Merrill - preparation for the generational wealth transfer: not found in the evidence provided. No Merrill or GWIM passage names the wealth transfer, heirs or next-gen client programs. Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America/Merrill investor day materials and GWIM earnings commentary on next-gen clients and heir retention

gaps.what: Raymond James - preparation for the generational wealth transfer: not found in the evidence provided. No Raymond James filing or call names wealth transfer or heirs; the only explicit 'intergenerational wealth strategies' reference is trade press.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James 10-K Item 1 and Private Client Group investor-day materials on next-gen clients and succession

gaps.what: Firm-specific estimates of transfer size, timing or share going to Gen X, millennials and women are not found for any of the five firms. Only Edward Jones (10-K) and Schwab (retention rate) refer to the transfer, and neither quantifies its size. The size and timing figures come from third-party research (Cerulli, UBS).
gaps.suggested_source: Firm investor presentations or proprietary client research on wealth-transfer exposure

gaps.what: Edward Jones - quantified heir-retention results: not found in the evidence provided. The firm cites outflows from generational wealth transfers outside the firm but gives no retention rate or heir-specific program data.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones earnings commentary or Partnership disclosures on Next Generation platform and client demographics
